barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt. Same comic job: the most grammatical speaker in the cast, formal register applied to small things, a status claim that cracks to show an earnest dork underneath. (Miranda's courtly-request shape is the secondary match, but the corpus has only one of her lines.) Bar 12: #2 intro; #10 '...a 360 degree spin from them! So disruptive!'; #26 'Save me from the consequences of my actions! Suggest an idea that lives up to my own hype!'; #27 'What kind of status could I post that would be idiot-proof?'; #28 'help me find an unpopular band to worship until pop culture inevitably ruins it'; #29 the time-machine sigh; #30 '3.85 billion BC, so you can be into existing before it was cool'; #31 'encountered a culinary block'; #32 'I have no reason to care about this, but suddenly it's all I care about! Someone stop this madness!'; #34 'vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst'; #35 'Liam? Beaming?'; #56 'no way anyone could ever be as cool as Liam'. Ours 12: 'Dear Valued Customer. No. Strike Customer.' / 'I have seen that line. I sent it in 2004.' / 'Brock, kindly lower your font size.' / 'By diplomatic courier, under armed escort and at no cost to yourself, my nightingale: my handwriting.' / 'Rest assured the treasury will match you pound for pound, while I, personally, hold your bag.' / 'Madam, with honourable intentions and an estate roughly the size of weather, I promise: home by ten.' / 'I wrote a love letter with no ask in it. It looked underdressed. I added a fee.' / 'Understood. I shall be in the drafts folder, where I am perfect.' / 'Persistence. My great-grandfather proposed by chain letter. It reached Portugal in March.' / '{star} likes {card}. I have bet a duchy on it, and not told the duchy.' / 'Please remove me from whatever list that was.' / 'Pick Vex. She will recommend you something wonderful. I know. I bought the placement.' VOICE (tie): covered, our best 12 are Prince by shape: the stacked courtesy clauses that pivot on a colon to a tiny want, the header/postscript form, the bureaucratic 'kindly'. Liam's are equally his (formal clause then a plea). But below the top 12 Prince's identity comes from spam nouns (attachment, unsubscribe, reply, folder), not shape; about a quarter of the bank loses him when you strip those words. CONSTRUCTION (tie): our best turns are tight and land on the last words ('my handwriting', 'home by ten', 'not told the duchy'), and they are tighter than Liam's #29 or #31. But Liam's #10 and #32 do something ours never does: the character is wrong or loses control in the act of speaking. QUOTABLE (bar): Liam's lines are clipped because they expose him ('worship until pop culture inevitably ruins it', the 180/360). Prince's best lines are clever remarks about spam, and his clever lines nearly all come from him knowing the joke. 'I sent it in 2004' and 'Strike Customer' are clippable. Most of the rest are wry asides, and the audience admires them without repeating them. Ours does not beat the bar on all three, so the bar wins.

templates: Template B, the lonely unread inbox, where Prince notices out loud that nobody replies or opens him (17 lines): 'Played {played}. Replies: one out-of-office...', 'She replied STOP... I still read it', 'never once been opened', 'It is in {star}'s junk folder', 'my auto-reply', 'to absolutely nobody', 'Your no has its own folder', 'A no, in your own words', 'I have copied in nobody tonight', 'far harder to raise', 'worth kidnapping', 'never once been accepted', 'I can see you typing no', 'I have never typed that before', 'nobody, at any point, asked about it', 'so I can believe it', 'marking it unread'. This is the worst template because it fills the beats that air every episode: confessions, closers, exit, win.

Template C, the spam stripped away to reveal sincerity ('for once without an offer', 'no fee' three times, 'Just Prince', 'sent once, by hand, with no follow-up') (6 lines). It is the same move as B, aimed at the star.

Template A, the vast royal asset filed as admin, then a colon or comma pivot to a 2 to 4 word small want (11 lines): sit next to me / one croissant and go / hold your bag / lunch, just us / my handwriting / home by ten / hello, you / say hi / one bench and your company / is on you / sit next to you. It is the persona's prescribed signature and produces the best lines in the bank. At 11 copies a regular viewer hears the colon and knows the turn is coming. Keep the best four and vary the rest.
Template D, the Subject:/Body:/Attachment: header skeleton (3 lines, two of them identical in form).

Recited-bible roasts: rival digs that restate the rival's CAST.md secret or flaw with a courtesy wrapper (Quill's last line, Crumb's empty slot and saved slice, Vex never recommended, Tilly unresolved and unable to hang up) (7 lines). The courtesy wrapper is Maximilian's, so the spam voice is missing.

Repeated phrases: 'paragraph nine' x2, 'never once' x2, 'in the strictest confidence' x2, 'sit next to' x2, 'four million' x2, 'by hand' x3, 'Reply all' x2, 'flip-flops' x2, 'archive(s)' x3, 'no fee' x3, 'in advance' x2 in the same twist.

Explains its own joke: 'Fireworks cannot talk.' (in the fear line), 'which I am told has never happened' (Vex roast), 'I did not know that was possible', 'I have never typed that before'.
List-like constructions (format-driven, borderline): the signature block 'Warm regards, Prince. Heir Apparent. Duke of the Western Moat. Single.' and 'Attachment one... Attachment two...'.

No em dashes, no emoji, no 'as an AI', no therapy talk, no brands or real people (Portugal is a place), nothing over PG-13 ('read posthumously' and 'worth kidnapping' are fine). Pet names ('my sweet', 'Beloved', 'Darling') are persona salutations, not stock filler.
biggestGap: Prince knows his own joke and narrates it: about 23 lines have him remark wistfully that nobody replies, opens or believes him. Every bar character is blind to their flaw (Liam botches the geometry while sounding clever, Vera's feminism comes out as an order). Next pass, delete the self-noticed-loneliness lines (templates B and C) and rewrite those beats so Prince sincerely believes spam is the highest form of courtship and is proud of it. He should treat an out-of-office as a love letter and a STOP as a strong open rate, so the audience sees the loneliness and he never says it.
